LESSON: VISUAL PROGRAMMING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Communication in Pre-Technical Studies
Topic 2.2: Visual Programming
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Visual Programming, part of Communication in Pre-Technical Studies in Grade 9 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are applications developed using visual programming software?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use print or digital media to search for information on the application areas of visual programming,
2. discuss the application areas of visual programming software,
3. watch a video on

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Visual Programming together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-Efficacy: effective communication skills are developed as the learner discusses the application areas of visual

programming with peers.

● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: open-mindedness and creativity skills are enhanced as the learner develops an

application using visual programming software.

Value:

● Social Justice: learner shares resources equitably with others when working in groups to develop applications.

● Responsibility: learner takes care of digital devices when developing interactive stories, games and animations using

visual programming software.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Peer Education and Mentorship: interpersonal relationships are enhanced as learner discusses the application areas of visual

programming software.

● Internet Safety and Security: responsible online behaviour is enhanced as learner uses digital media to search for information

on the application areas of visual programming.

Link to other Subjects

Creative Arts and Sports: learner enhances skills of animations when developing interactive stories and games.
